name: Anangu religion (Tjukurpa)

dating.dating_summary: Western Desert regional occupation is dated to ~35,000-47,830 BP (Puritjarra rock shelter) but this is regional-occupation evidence, not a date for Uluru-specific ceremonial content — official park sources themselves state the exact age of Uluru's own rock art is unknown; earliest outsider attestation begins with Gosse's 1873 naming and intensifies with Mountford (1940s-60s) and Layton (1977-79) fieldwork; no valid method exists to date specific currently-practiced Tjukurpa narrative content.

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: Puritjarra rock shelter (Cleland Hills), excavated by Mike Smith: continuous occupation from ~35,000 years ago, earlier signs to ~45,000 years; rock-art pigment production dated to ~13,000 BP at earliest. This is regional Western Desert evidence, not Uluru-specific. Official park sources state explicitly: "the exact age of the rock-art [at Uluru] is unknown" — popular tourism-source claims of "30,000+ years continuous occupation" specifically at Uluru were not traced to any peer-reviewed primary citation and should not be used.

earliest_written_attestation.note: Explorer William Gosse named "Ayers Rock" in 1873 (European written contact, not ethnographic documentation). Sustained ethnographic documentation begins with Charles P. Mountford's fieldwork, 1940s-60s (Ayers Rock: Its People, Their Beliefs and Their Art, 1965), and intensively with Robert Layton's fieldwork 1977-79 for the land claim (Uluru: An Aboriginal History of Ayers Rock, Aboriginal Studies Press, 1986).

tradition_internal_claim.note: Anangu's own public-facing materials (via jointly-managed Parks Australia) state there is no word for "Dreamtime" in Anangu languages and explicitly reject "dream" as a gloss; Tjukurpa asserts ancestral beings shaped land/law in a time that functions as an ongoing structuring principle, continuously practiced and renewed, not a frozen ancient artifact with a calendar date.

estimated_oral_origin.method: No defensible method exists to date specific currently-practiced Tjukurpa narrative content (e.g. the Kuniya/Liru story cycle) against the ~35,000-45,000-year regional occupation record; conflating regional deep-time occupation with the age of a specific story is explicitly flagged by this research as an error to avoid.

notes: Tjukurpa functions simultaneously as cosmology (ancestral-being creation stories), law, and moral/social order — per Anangu's own stated framing via Parks Australia and DCCEEW materials. Prefer "Law" or the untranslated term over "Dreaming" per Anangu's own documented preference.
